record.paper_title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
record.original_question: When Heine-Stieltjes polynomial zeros yield only critical configurations of the discrete energy rather than global minimizers, can one prove that the corresponding discrete critical measures converge in the thermodynamic limit to continuous critical measures, and that every continuous critical measure in the class can be obtained in this way?

evidence.quote: two open problems remain: (i) to prove that discrete critical measures converge in the thermodynamic limit to continuous critical measures, and that all continuous critical measures can be obtained this way;

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{p}(z-a_j)$ be a polynomial of degree $p+1$ with distinct fixed complex zeros $a_0,\dots,a_p$, and let positive "charges" $\nu_0,\dots,\nu_p>0$ be assigned to these points. For each positive integer $n$, a Heine–Stieltjes polynomial of degree $n$ is a polynomial $y_n(z)$ for which there exists a polynomial $V_n(z)$ (the corresponding Van Vleck polynomial) of degree $\le p-1$ such that
$$A(z)\,y_n''(z)+\Big(\sum_{j=0}^{p}\frac{\nu_j\,A(z)}{z-a_j}\Big)y_n'(z)-V_n(z)\,y_n(z)=0.$$
Equivalently, the zeros $z_1,\dots,z_n$ of $y_n$ are critical points of the discrete logarithmic energy
$$E_n(x_1,\dots,x_n)=-\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}\log|x_i-x_j|-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=0}^{p}\nu_j\log|x_i-a_j|,$$
i.e. solutions of $\sum_{k\ne i}\frac{1}{z_i-z_k}+\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{p}\frac{\nu_j}{z_i-a_j}=0$ for all $i$. (When the configuration is a global minimum, classical Stieltjes theory applies; here general critical—possibly saddle—configurations are allowed.) Associate to such a configuration the normalized discrete zero-counting measure $\mu_n=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{z_i}$.

A finite positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}$ of total mass $1$ is called a continuous critical measure (with external field generated by $A$ and weights $\nu_j$) if for every smooth compactly supported vector field $h$ on $\mathbb{C}\setminus\{a_0,\dots,a_p\}$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Big(\iint\log\frac{1}{|(z+th(z))-(w+th(w))|}d\mu(z)d\mu(w)+\sum_{j=0}^{p}\nu_j\!\int\log\frac{1}{|z+th(z)-a_j|}d\mu(z)\Big)=0.$$

Fix a sequence of total charges with $n\to\infty$ in such a way that the ratios $\nu_j/n$ tend to prescribed positive constants (the thermodynamic scaling). Prove the following two assertions:
(a) Any weak-$*$ accumulation point of a sequence $(\mu_n)$ of normalized zero-counting measures of Heine–Stieltjes polynomials, taken along this scaling, is a continuous critical measure.
(b) Conversely, every continuous critical measure arising in this electrostatic class is the weak-$*$ limit of some such sequence $(\mu_n)$ of discrete critical measures.
artifact.category_tag: Logarithmic potential theory and Heine–Stieltjes polynomials
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Martínez-Finkelshtein and Rakhmanov established direction (a): weak-$*$ limits of zero-counting measures of Heine–Stieltjes polynomials are continuous critical measures, characterized via quadratic differentials with closed trajectories. The converse direction (b)—that every continuous critical measure in the class is realized as such a limit—does not appear to be fully settled in the literature, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Critical measures, quadratic differentials, and weak limits of zeros of Stieltjes polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: A weak-* limit of a sequence of discrete critical measures is a continuous critical measure; limit zero distributions of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials are given by continuous critical measures.
status_evidence.claim: Direction (a) — convergence of discrete critical measures from Heine–Stieltjes zeros to continuous critical measures — is established.

status_evidence.title: A Law of Large Numbers for the Zeroes of Heine–Stieltjes Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Determines the limiting density of zeros in the thermodynamic limit, proving a strong law of large numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Limiting zero distributions exist in the thermodynamic limit for relevant cases.

status_evidence.title: Heine–Stieltjes polynomials (Wikipedia)
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial solutions of a Fuchsian second-order ODE associated with the Stieltjes electrostatic problem.
status_evidence.claim: Basic setup and definitions of the polynomials are standard.
